chapter_notes: H430 'Elohim' consistently takes singular verbs throughout this chapter (bara, vayomer, vayar, vayavdel, vayiqra, vaya'as, vayitten, vayevarekh). This singular verb agreement demonstrates that the ים- suffix functions as an intensifier rather than a numerical plural. The sole exception is verse 26 ('na'aseh' — 'let us make'), where the verb shifts to 1st person plural. This anomaly is textually significant and preserved as-is.
The refrain 'and there was evening and there was morning' closes each day. Note: evening precedes morning, establishing the Hebrew day-cycle as beginning at dusk.

The verb 'bara' (H1254, to create) appears only at three points: verse 1 (sky and earth), verse 21 (sea creatures and living things), and verse 27 (humanity — three times). All other acts of making use 'asah' (H6213, to make/do). This distinction may be intentional, with 'bara' reserved for genuinely new categories of existence.

The pattern 'and God said...and it was so...and God saw that it was good' structures the entire chapter. Day two notably lacks 'and God saw that it was good,' while day three receives two such declarations, and day six climaxes with 'exceedingly good.'

H5315 'nephesh' — consistently rendered 'breath' or 'breathing thing' throughout this chapter rather than 'soul.' The word's primary meaning is concrete: the breathing life-force that animates creatures. The abstract/spiritual connotation that 'soul' carries in English is not present in the Hebrew of Genesis 1.

Genesis 1:1: H430 'elohim' — singular verb 'bara' (Qal perfect 3ms) governs a morphologically plural noun. The ים- ending here functions as an intensifier ('the Mighty One,' 'the Fullness of God') rather than a numerical plural, as demonstrated by the singular verb throughout this chapter.
H8064 'shamayim' rendered 'sky' per word study finding: the physical sky/expanse above, from a root meaning 'to be lofty.' The ים- ending functions as intensifying rather than pluralizing.
H853 'et' (object marker) appears twice — untranslatable in English but marks 'the sky' and 'the earth' as definite direct objects.
Genesis 1:2: H1961 'hayetah' — Qal perfect 3fs. Often rendered 'was,' but hayah is emphatic in Hebrew (not a mere copula). 'Had become' captures the completed-action force. Whether the earth was created in this state or became so is a long-standing interpretive question; the verb itself supports both readings.
H8414 'tohu' — desolation, wasteland, formlessness. Rendered 'waste' rather than 'without form' for directness.

H7307 'ruach' — the semantic range (spirit/wind/breath) is genuinely active here. The Piel participle 'merachephet' (hovering/brooding) suggests animate agency, favoring 'spirit,' but the physical image of wind over water is also present.
H7363 'merachephet' — Piel participle feminine singular, matching 'ruach.' Means 'hovering' or 'brooding' (as a bird over its nest, cf. Deut 32:11). Rendered 'hovering' rather than KJV 'moved.'
H4325 'mayim' — rendered 'water' (singular sense) per the principle that the ים- ending on this word is inherent to the noun, not a numerical plural.
Genesis 1:3: H1961 'yehi' — Qal jussive 3ms, expressing a command/will: 'let there be.' The waw-consecutive 'vayehi' that follows reports the completed result.
Genesis 1:4: H914 'vayavdel' — Hiphil waw-consecutive 3ms: 'caused to separate.' Rendered 'separated' for readability. The Hiphil stem indicates God actively caused the division.
Genesis 1:5: H259 'echad' — 'one' rather than 'first' (which would be 'rishon'). The Hebrew says 'day one,' not 'the first day.' This is notable because the ordinal form is used for days two through six. 'Day one' may carry special significance — a unified, singular day.
Genesis 1:6: H7549 'raqia' — from 'raqa' (to beat/spread out). Rendered 'expanse' rather than KJV 'firmament' (which comes via Latin 'firmamentum'). The Hebrew describes something spread out or stretched, not necessarily something solid.
H914 'mavdil' — Hiphil participle: 'causing separation.' Rendered as 'separating' to show the ongoing participial function.
Genesis 1:8: H8064 'shamayim' — here used as the name given to the expanse, rendered 'Sky' to match verse 1. Note that the raqia (expanse) is what God names 'shamayim,' identifying the visible sky-dome with this word.
Genesis 1:9: H6960 'yiqqavu' — Niphal jussive 3mp: 'let them be gathered together.' The root qavah means 'to bind together, collect.' The related noun 'miqveh' (gathering/collection) appears in the next verse.
H7200 'teraeh' — Niphal imperfect 3fs: 'let it be seen/appear.' The dry ground is the subject — it passively appears as the water recedes.
Genesis 1:10: H4723 'miqveh' — 'gathering, collection.' Related to the verb qavah in the previous verse. The word also means 'hope' elsewhere in Scripture (e.g., Jer 17:13), creating a notable semantic link between 'gathering of waters' and 'hope.'
Genesis 1:11: H1876/H1877 'tadshé...deshe' — the verb and noun share the same root, creating a figure: 'let the earth sprout sprouts.' This cognate accusative construction is characteristic of Hebrew and worth preserving.
H1876 'tadshé' — morphologically Hiphil jussive 3fs: 'let it cause to sprout.' The earth is commanded to actively produce.
Genesis 1:12: H3318 'vattotsé' — Hiphil waw-consecutive 3fs: 'and it caused to go out / brought forth.' The earth actively produces in response to God's command.
Genesis 1:14: H3974 'me'orot' — 'luminaries, light-bearers.' Distinct from 'or' (light) in verse 3. These are light-bearing bodies, not light itself.

H4150 'mo'adim' — 'appointed times.' Often rendered 'seasons' (KJV), but the word specifically means appointed meetings or fixed occasions. This is the same word used for Israel's festival calendar (Lev 23). Rendered 'appointed times' to preserve this connection.
Genesis 1:15: H215 'leha'ir' — Hiphil infinitive construct: 'to cause to shine / to give light.' The Hiphil stem shows causative function.
Genesis 1:16: H4475 'memsheleth' — 'governance, dominion, rule.' Rendered 'governance' rather than KJV 'rule' to capture the institutional/structural sense of the noun form (as distinct from the verb 'mashal').

The text does not name the sun or moon — it calls them 'the great luminary' and 'the small luminary.' This may be deliberate, avoiding the names of celestial bodies that were worshipped as deities in the ancient Near East.
Genesis 1:17: H5414 'vayitten' — Qal waw-consecutive 3ms: 'and he gave/placed/set.' The primary meaning is 'to give,' but in context 'placed' captures the action of positioning the luminaries.
Genesis 1:20: H5315 'nephesh' — 'breathing creature, living being.' The word means literally 'a breather' — that which breathes. Rendered 'breath' here in construct with 'living' (nephesh chayyah = 'living breath/being'). This is the same word often translated 'soul' elsewhere, but its primary meaning is concrete: a breathing creature.
H8317/H8318 'yishretsu...sherets' — another cognate accusative: 'let them swarm swarms.' The verb and noun share the same root.
H5774 'ye'opheph' — Polel imperfect 3ms: intensive/repetitive flying. The doubled stem suggests continuous or vigorous flight.
Genesis 1:21: H8577 'tanninim' — 'sea creatures, sea monsters.' The word can mean dragon, serpent, whale, or any great marine creature. Rendered 'sea creatures' as the most neutral translation of the literal sense. KJV 'whales' is too specific.

H7430 'haromeset' — Qal participle feminine singular with article: 'the gliding/creeping one.' Rendered 'that glides' to capture the swift, smooth movement implied by the root (ramas = to glide swiftly).
H3671 'kanaph' — 'wing.' The construct 'oph kanaph' is literally 'bird of wing,' meaning 'winged bird.'
Genesis 1:22: H1288 'vayevarekh' — Piel waw-consecutive 3ms: 'and he blessed.' The Piel stem intensifies the action — an emphatic, deliberate blessing.
Genesis 1:24: H929 'behemah' — 'beast, livestock.' From a root probably meaning 'to be mute.' Refers to large domesticated quadrupeds. Rendered 'livestock' for clarity.
H2416 appears twice in this verse with different morphological forms: first as an adjective (chayyah, 'living') modifying nephesh, then as a noun in construct (chayyeto, 'living thing of').
Genesis 1:25: H127 'adamah' — 'ground, soil.' Distinguished from 'erets' (earth/land). The adamah is the cultivable soil, the red earth from which adam (humanity) takes its name.
Genesis 1:26: H120 'adam' — 'humanity, humankind.' From the root 'adam' (to be red), related to 'adamah' (ground/soil). Rendered 'humanity' here because the context is the creation of the species, not yet the individual man named Adam.
H6754 'tselem' — 'image, representative figure.' The word implies a representative likeness — as a statue represents a king.
H1823 'demuth' — 'likeness, resemblance.' Complementary to 'tselem' but emphasizes similarity/pattern rather than representative image.

H6213 'na'aseh' — Qal imperfect 1st common plural: 'let us make.' The shift to first person plural is textually significant and has generated extensive commentary. The translation preserves the Hebrew as-is.
H7287 'yirdu' — Qal jussive 3mp: 'and let them rule/have dominion.' The root radah means 'to tread down, to exercise dominion.'
Genesis 1:27: H1254 'bara' appears three times in this verse — a striking triple emphasis. The verb is Qal perfect 3ms each time: completed, decisive action.
H120 'ha-adam' — with the article here: 'the human/the adam.' Rendered 'the human' to distinguish from the generic 'humanity' in verse 26.

The poetic structure is tripartite: (1) God created the human in his image, (2) in God's image he created him, (3) male and female he created them. The shift from singular 'him' to plural 'them' is present in the Hebrew.
Genesis 1:28: H3533 'kivshuha' — Qal imperative 2mp with 3fs suffix: 'subdue it.' The root kavash means 'to tread down, conquer, bring into subjection.' A strong word — humanity is given active authority over the earth.
Genesis 1:29: H2009 'hinneh' — 'Look! Behold!' A presentative particle drawing attention. Rendered 'Look' for directness rather than archaic 'Behold.'
Genesis 1:30: H3418 'yereq' — 'green, verdure.' Refers to the green color of vegetation. Rendered 'green' as an adjective modifying 'plant.'
The verb 'I have given' from verse 29 carries forward grammatically into verse 30 — God's gift of green plants as food applies to all living, breathing creatures.
Genesis 1:31: H3966 'me'od' — 'exceedingly, very.' From a root suggesting vehemence or intensity. Here it intensifies 'good' — not merely good, but forcefully, emphatically good.

Unlike days 1–5, 'the sixth day' (yom hashishi) has the definite article on the ordinal number. This is the only day in Genesis 1 where the ordinal is made definite with the article, possibly marking it as climactic.
